Who this worksheet is for

This worksheet helps Year 9 learners turn stated angle facts into linear equations. It connects geometry knowledge with algebra rather than treating the two skills separately.

Four lesson and exercise pages are followed by two solution pages covering all six exercise groups. Activities include choosing an angle fact, explaining an error, finding a missing angle expression and checking all angles.

6 pages · Examples, practice & solutions

What the worksheet covers

  • Triangle angles totalling 180°
  • Adjacent angles on a straight line totalling 180°
  • Angles around a point totalling 360°
  • Quadrilateral interior angles totalling 360°
  • Equal angles in an isosceles triangle
  • Missing expressions, error spotting and independent checking

Prerequisites: basic angle facts and solving linear equations. Problems are text-based, with angle expressions stated in words rather than geometry diagrams. Exercise 2(c) intentionally gives a fractional value. This is a focused KS3 classroom worksheet, not a full geometry course or an official exam-board paper.

Key ideas at a glance

Choose the angle fact before forming an equation

A triangle's interior angles total 180°, whereas angles around a point total 360°. Add the given angle expressions and set them equal to the appropriate total.

Check the angles after solving

Substitute the value of x into each angle expression. For the final quadrilateral problem, x = 50 gives 60°, 120°, 80° and 100°, which total 360°.
